# Session 1

Preparation, installation, launch!

See https://isee.github.io/iUSEiSEE/articles/d01_preparation.html

## Exercises - session 1

I would like you to do the following:

* Load the `sce_pbmc3k` dataset from the iUSEiSEE package

```{r}
sce_pbmc3k <- readRDS(
  file = system.file("datasets", "sce_pbmc3k.RDS", package = "iUSEiSEE")
)

sce_pbmc3k
```


* See what else is there in the `iUSEiSEE` package

I am checking out https://github.com/iSEE/iUSEiSEE

We have...

- vignettes
- the datasets to be used

* Load the iSEE package and start its main example

```{r}
library(scRNAseq)

# Example data ----
sce <- ReprocessedAllenData(assays="tophat_counts")
class(sce)

library(scrapper)
sce <- normalizeRnaCounts.se(sce, assay.type = "tophat_counts")

library(scater)
sce <- runPCA(sce, ncomponents=4)
sce <- runTSNE(sce)
rowData(sce)$ave_count <- rowMeans(assay(sce, "tophat_counts"))
rowData(sce)$n_cells <- rowSums(assay(sce, "tophat_counts") > 0)
sce

```


* Have a first look at the iSEE app - it is fully up and running!

```{r}
library("iSEE")
iSEE(se = sce)
```


* Find out which parameters in the main `iSEE()` function are used to control...
  - the configuration with which the app starts

# Session 3

Exploration, done for real and in-depth, with iSEE  
... with a keen eye on working in a reproducible manner

https://isee.github.io/iUSEiSEE/articles/d02_iSEE_overview.html

## Exercises - session 3

I would like you to do the following, using the `sce_pbmc3k` dataset:

* Organize the iSEE panels:
  - Search for the `Organize panels` button. 
  - Try to add and remove panels, and resize and reorder the existing ones.
  - Remember to click on `Apply settings` afterwards. 
  
Well. do as it says, and possibly remember that you can *always* have the `initial` configuration cleverly scripted!
 

* Multiple panels of the same type:
  - Show three _Reduced dimension plot_ panels; one showing the PCA representation, one showing the t-SNE representation.
  - Link them together, so that points that are selected in one are highlighted in the other.
  - Change the coloring to use two different genes which could be marker of some specific cell types.
  
```{r}
iSEE(sce, initial = list(ReducedDimensionPlot(),
                         ReducedDimensionPlot(),
                         ReducedDimensionPlot()))
```
  
From any of the panels, have the "Color by" field select "by feature name", and in there choose any gene by simply typing it in - or even passing it on from e.g. a RowDataTable plot!

* More on `iSEE` links and transmissions:
  - Start an instance with the default set of panels and explore the different types of plots generated by the Feature assay plot panel using the choices available for the two axes.
  - Select a set of points in one of the _Feature assay plot_ panels, by drawing a rectangle around them. 
  - Then open the _Selection parameters_ collapsible box of another _Feature assay plot_, or a _Column data plot_ panel, and select the _Feature assay plot_ panel where you made the point selection from the dropdown menu under **Receive column selection from**. 
  - Note how the points corresponding to the cells that you selected in the first panel are highlighted in the receiving panel. 
  - You can highlight the points in different ways by changing the **Selection effect**.
  - Find the Examine panel chart control and obtain a graphical representation of the app configuration
  
```{r}
iSEE(sce_pbmc3k, initial = list(FeatureAssayPlot(width = 3),
                                ColumnDataPlot(width = 3),
                                FeatureAssayPlot(width = 3),
                                RowDataTable(width = 3)))
```
  
  

* Color the points:
  - Open the `Visual parameters` collapsible box in one of the _Reduced dimension plot_ panels, and set `Color by:` to `Column data`.
  - Color the cells by `Cluster`, which contains the cluster labels that were assigned to the cells in the preprocessing step.
  - Color the cells by the log10-transformed number of detected genes (`log10_total`).
  - Set `Color by:` to `Feature name` in one of the _Reduced dimension plot_ panels, and select one of the genes from the dropdown menu. You can search for a gene of interest by typing in the dropdown box.
  
```{r}
iSEE(sce_pbmc3k, initial = list(ReducedDimensionPlot(),
                                ReducedDimensionPlot()))
```
  

* Highlight & zoom:
  - Set `Color by:` to `Sample name` in one of the Reduced dimension plots, and use the dropdown menu underneath to change the highlighted cell.
  - Reduce the point size and increase the transparency (i.e., reduce the value for the alpha attribute).
  - Apply a downsampling grid of 100 horizontal and vertical bins.
  - As above, select a region in the first panel and transmit the selection to the second one.
  - Double-click on the area selected in the first panel to zoom and display the same view as the second panel.
  - Double click again anywhere in the panel to zoom out.
  
No need to code too much on this, "just follow along"  

* Launch iSEE with pre-specified configurations:
  - Start `iSEE` in the default configuration.
  - Click on the export icon in the top-right corner, and select 'Display panel settings'.
  - Copy all the code shown in the pop-up window. 
  - Close the app and paste this code in your R session.
  - This defines the 'initial' list. Then launch a new instance adding `initial = initial` to the `iSEE` call. 
  - Note how the app starts in the same configuration as it was before closing. Of course, it is still possible to continue exploring the data interactively - we have only changed the starting configuration.
  - Start `iSEE` with one _Column data plot_ and one _Row data plot_ panel.
  - Start `iSEE` in an empty configuration.
  
```{r}
## custom config
#### basically select any app config you might want to put together!



## just two panels
iSEE(sce_pbmc3k, initial = list(ColumnDataPlot(), RowDataPlot()))

## empty config
iSEE(sce_pbmc3k, initial = list())
# oooor 
iSEEu::modeEmpty(sce_pbmc3k)
# oooor 
## You open up the app live in any configuration AND delete the panels as you go

```

If needing to use iSEE as a server:

```{r}
options(shiny.maxRequestSize = 100 * 1024^2)
```

could be set to upload e.g. files sized up to 100Mb (adapt the number if needed)
  

* Export code to (re)create the exact output:
  - Click on the export icon in the top-right corner, and select 'Extract the R code'.
  - Copy the preamble and the code for the first plot from the pop-up window. Close the app and paste the code in your R session.
  - Note how this recreates the plots from the app - you can render the copied code in a Rmd/qmd notebook and obtain a full document. 
  
Copypasting the code in a fresh notebook or script, and executing it again - Check that the intermediate `dot.plot` and other output elements are showing what you were plotting.
If needed/in a quarto/knitr notebook, remember to adjust the `fig.width` and `fig.height` to control the true size and aspect of the generated output!

Obvious suggestion: 
* Enter the lab meeting with iSEE and a compelling configuration on (and stored)
* Listen to the feedback of your colleagues and PIs
* Adapt the configuration as you go
* Store the final configuration as another `initial` object
* Rinse & repeat!
* ... soon get to the configuration where you will deploy your dataset!

* iSEEDE & iSEEpathways

This follows the content of the vignette

```{r}
library(iSEE)
library(iSEEde)
library(iSEEpathways)
library(iUSEiSEE)

sce_macrophage <- readRDS(
  system.file("datasets", "sce_macrophage_readytouse.RDS",
              package = "iUSEiSEE")
)

sce_macrophage

library("iSEE")
library("iSEEde")
library("iSEEpathways")
library("AnnotationDbi")
library("org.Hs.eg.db")
library("GO.db")

app <- iSEE(sce_macrophage, 
            initial = list(
              ReducedDimensionPlot(PanelWidth = 3L),
              iSEEde::DETable(
                PanelWidth = 3L,
                ContrastName = "IFNgTRUE.SL1344TRUE.DESeq2",
                HiddenColumns = c("baseMean", "lfcSE", "stat")
              ),
              iSEEde::VolcanoPlot(PanelWidth = 3L,
                                  ContrastName = "IFNgTRUE.SL1344TRUE.DESeq2"),
              iSEEde::MAPlot(PanelWidth = 3L,
                             ContrastName = "IFNgTRUE.SL1344TRUE.DESeq2"),
              PathwaysTable(
                ResultName = "IFNgTRUE.SL1344TRUE.limma.fgsea",
                Selected = "GO:0046324"
              ),
              ComplexHeatmapPlot(
                RowSelectionSource = "PathwaysTable1",
                CustomRows = FALSE, ColumnData = "condition_name",
                ClusterRows = TRUE, Assay = "vst"
              ),
              FgseaEnrichmentPlot(
                ResultName = "IFNgTRUE.SL1344TRUE.limma.fgsea",
                PathwayId = "GO:0046324"
              )
            ))

app


```

* iSEEindex & iSEEhub

Basic example to expand upon - yaml provided within iSEEindex itself

```{r}
library("iSEE")
library("iSEEindex")
library("BiocFileCache")

bfc <- BiocFileCache(cache = tempdir())

dataset_fun <- function() {
  x <- yaml::read_yaml(system.file(package = "iSEEindex", "example.yaml"))
  x$datasets
}
initial_fun <- function() {
  x <- yaml::read_yaml(system.file(package = "iSEEindex", "example.yaml"))
  x$initial
}
app <- iSEEindex(bfc, dataset_fun, initial_fun)
```

* Again using the `sce_pbmc3k` dataset, use the `iSEE_init()` from iSEEfier to get the exploration started

```{r}
library("iSEEfier")

# import data
sce <- readRDS(
  file = system.file("datasets", "sce_pbmc3k.RDS", package = "iUSEiSEE")
)

sce

# define the list of genes
feature_list_1 <- c("GZMB", "TGFB1", "CD28")
# define the cluster/cell type 
cluster_1 <- "labels_main"

initial_1 <- iSEEinit(sce,
                      features = feature_list_1,
                      clusters = cluster_1,
                      add_markdown_panel = TRUE)

iSEEfier::view_initial_tiles(initial_1)

iSEEfier::view_initial_network(initial_1)

iSEE(sce, initial = initial_1)
```


* Also from iSEEfier, try out the `iSEEmarker()` function - before starting the app, check out its initial configuration with the `view_initial_...` functions

```{r}
sce

mark_init <- iSEEmarker(sce = sce, 
                        clusters = "labels_main", 
                        groups = "labels_main",
                        selection_plot_format = "ColumnDataPlot")
mark_init
view_initial_tiles(mark_init)

iSEE(sce, initial = mark_init)

glue_initials(mark_init, initial_1) |> view_initial_tiles()

```

## Exercises - session 6

I would like you to do the following, with the `sce_pbmc3k` dataset: 

* Check out the tour drafter functionality from the upper control bar in iSEE

```{r}
iSEE(sce)

my_tour <- read.delim("myfirsttour.txt", sep = ";")
iSEE(sce, initial = list(ReducedDimensionPlot(), 
                         ReducedDimensionPlot(), 
                         ReducedDimensionPlot()), tour = my_tour)
```

Let's see how the elements are called in the UI

Keep in mind it is provided as semicolon-separated text, use `read-delim(..., sep = "";)`

The cherry on top:

* Take literally *any* dataset you might have on your laptop (they can even be Seurat objects or AnnData objects coming from Scanpy/scverse), start exploring that within iSEE, show it around and be damn proud of it!

```{r}

```

Some good inspiration sources:

- iSEE_KDM6B (classical SCE) --> https://shiny.imbei.uni-mainz.de/iSEE_KDM6B_inhibition/
- iSEE on complement data (SCE from Seurat) --> https://shiny.imbei.uni-mainz.de/iSEE_complement/
- iSEE_TICA (uses a scanpy h5ad file) --> https://shiny.imbei.uni-mainz.de/iSEE_TICA

Remember the trick to keep as .h5 file, compatible with Bioc - it speeds up the loading phase big time

Also: zellkonverter AND anndataR can be your best friends for converting!

BTW: look what others, not just we, have done with iSEE --> https://isee.github.io/apps.html

Thank you all for making it such a beautiful and exciting workshop!
